Basking on the stony beaches of the Sol’Kesh coasts, the daugon is a survivor of two extreme temperature dualities. Found deep along 
the ocean floor, protected by a layer in thick blubber to withstand the frigid depths in which it scavenges for mollusks. By high noon, the 
large mammal will then rise to the surface, chewing through coastal plants while basking in the heat of the sun. When laying out on the 
beach, a dorsal sail arches upward, helping warm its blood to once again return to the depths. Th e striking colors of the sail's sunburst 
pattern is only found on males as they are used as a display towards potential mates. Th e matriarchal herd mothers often have their pick 
of competing males during the warm summer season and the bright colors make for a robust male to pick.

Encountering Rather docile when resting in the sun or chewing 
terrestrial plants, the daugon is only ever aggressive to others 
when the herd is being harassed; both males and females 
will fi rst raise their sails and hoot loudly as a warning. An 
approaching Traveler can appease them by offering fresh sea 
grass in a slow peaceful manner, but any movement towards 
their pups will lead to an immediate and aggressive assault.
